newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Ford sees breaking even in Vietnam by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Ford sees breaking even in Vietnam by 2000.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. said Friday it expects to break even in Vietnam by the year 2000 despite what analysts say is an overcrowded market.

In an interview in Hanoi, Ford Executive Vice President Wayne Booker dismissed industry concerns over problems facing manufacturers in Vietnam and said the company's first locally made vehicle would roll off the production line within a year.
Hanoi has licensed 14 foreign manufacturers, including Ford, to produce vehicles in Vietnam for the local market. Current demand for new cars is barely 10,000 units a year.
But Booker said Ford's $102 million plant, now being built near Hanoi, would produce commercial vehicles rather than passenger cars until the market was better developed.
"It will break even before 2000," he said. "Any manufacturer who can't make profits by 2000 oughtn't be here."

Booker said a new light, inexpensive mini-car, could be appropriate for Vietnam, but only after 2000. Ford said at the Paris auto show earlier this week that the mini-car was being studied for developing markets,
Vietnam's auto market is now dominated by Japanese and South Korean marques including Nissan, Mitsubishi, Daewoo and Kia.
